title: Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · para0010】However, tumors abutting the bowel remain a major challenge in SBRT. According to the 2025 National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Kidney Cancer, tumors abutting the bowel should not be considered amenable to SBRT.10 However, methods that create sufficient separation between the tumor and bowel, such as emerging spacer technologies, may help expand the applicability of SBRT in selected cases. The clinical utility of these spacers depends on achieving a stable and sufficient separation within the retroperitoneum, which has not yet been thoroughly evaluated. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of computed tomography (CT)-guided placement of hydrogel spacers at different retroperitoneal sites using cadaveric models and to explore its potential dosimetric impact on the perirenal space.

【Purpose · abstract-1-1】Hydrogel spacers reduce the rectal radiation dose and toxicity in prostate cancer radiation therapy. However, their use in other malignancies, including renal cell carcinoma (RCC), remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the feasibility of hydrogel spacer placement at different retroperitoneal sites and its potential dosimetric effects during stereotactic body radiation therapy for RCC using cadaveric models.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and setting · para0011】This cadaveric study was conducted at Okayama University. All donors provided written informed consent for body donation for medical education and research. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by our institutional ethics committee (approval number: K2309-026).

【Methods and materials · abstract-2-1】Hydrogel spacers were percutaneously administered under computed tomography (CT) guidance to 3 cadavers at the following retroperitoneal sites: (1) the perirenal space, (2) the perivascular region of the iliac vessels, and (3) the iliacus muscle region. Spacer stability and separation distance from organs at risk were evaluated using CT images acquired immediately after placement, at 1 week, and at 1 to 2 months. The dosimetric effect was assessed in the perirenal spacer case by comparing radiation treatment plans for a simulated RCC lesion generated before and after spacer placement using a treatment planning system.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space achieved a stable separation of approximately 1 cm between the kidney and bowel, which was maintained at the 1-month follow-up. The perivascular spacer failed to maintain its shape at the time of placement and became indistinguishable on the follow-up CT, whereas the iliacus muscle spacer remained stable but provided limited bowel separation. Treatment planning showed a reduction in bowel dose in the perirenal case, with the maximum dose to the small intestine reduced by 9.6% and to the large intestine by 35.9%.

【Conclusions · para0027】This exploratory cadaveric study identified distinct patterns of hydrogel spacer behavior across different retroperitoneal compartments. Stable spacer retention and maintained separation were observed in the perirenal space, whereas spacer collapse occurred in the perivascular region, and anatomically stable but potentially less clinically relevant separation was observed in the iliacus region. In a single simulated RCC SBRT scenario, perirenal spacer placement was associated with reduced bowel dose. These preliminary findings suggest that local anatomic characteristics may influence hydrogel spacer stability within the retroperitoneum and identify the perirenal space as a potentially favorable anatomic environment for further investigation. Additional preclinical and clinical studies are required to determine whether these observations translate into clinically meaningful benefits for living patients.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · fig0001】Figure 1 Axial computed tomography images of hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space. The hydrogel spacer, small intestine, and large intestine are contoured and displayed with translucent fills in cyan, orange, and yellow, respectively. The spacer is successfully positioned in the perirenal space immediately after placement (A). A stable separation of approximately 1 cm between the kidney and adjacent bowel was maintained at 1 week (B) and 1 month (C) after placement, with minimal morphologic changes observed during follow-up.

【Figure 2 · fig0002】Figure 2 Axial computed tomography images of hydrogel spacer placement in the iliacus muscle region. The hydrogel spacer is contoured and displayed with a translucent fill in cyan. The spacer is successfully placed in the iliacus muscle region immediately after placement (A). An apparent increase in spacer volume is observed 1 week after placement (B). The spacer remains identifiable 1.5 months after placement (C).

【Figure 3 · fig0003】Figure 3 Axial computed tomography (CT) images and volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) dose distributions before and after hydrogel spacer placement. (A) Axial CT image before spacer placement in the perirenal space. (B) Dose distribution from the VMAT plan based on the pre-spacer CT. (C) Axial CT image at 1 month after spacer placement in the perirenal space. (D) Dose distribution from the VMAT plan based on the post-spacer CT at 1 month. The hydrogel spacer, virtual renal cell carcinoma, planning target volume, small intestine, and large intestine are contoured with translucent fills in cyan, red, light green, orange, and yellow, respectively. Isodose lines represent percentages relative to the prescribed dose. High-dose exposure to the bowel structures is reduced in the post-spacer plan (D), while adequate planning target volume coverage is maintained.
